text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The president is consulting with the ruling coalition parties and may appoint Mart Siimann as candidate to the premier's as early as today.
- Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov declared that Russia will never accept the admission of the Baltic states to NATO.
- A programme for the prevention of juvenile crime has ben approved and will be submitted to the government.
- The current system of paying transport subsidies to students allows cheating and officials do not expect the allocated funds to be enough.
- An article analysed land price differences in Estonia: one square metre in central Tallinn may cost up to 5,000 kroons and less than one kroon in remote villages.
- Estonia's basketball team lost to Latvia.
- The daily interviewed Estonian Ambassador to the U.K. Raul Maelk. The ambassador recommended that an office of the Estonian Investment Agency be opened in London.
- Securities specialists predict that the price rise of shares at the Tallinn exchange will continue.
- The Roads Department will present today the latest version of the Tallinn-Tartu motorway.
- The Bank of Estonia will sell its 17 percent share of the Savings Bank to avoid a conflict of interests.
